title: BWF Shuttle Time — movement foundations
attribution: Badminton World Federation, Shuttle Time Teachers’ Manual, Module 5; short paraphrase reviewed against federation-hosted manual.
text: BWF beginner teaching introduces ready position, split steps, chasse steps and lunges as movement foundations. Progress from simpler movements to combined footwork. A coach can adapt the lesson to ability and available space. This does not establish a player's mistake from a video or provide rehabilitation.

title: AIS — training and competition nutrition
attribution: Australian Institute of Sport; short paraphrase of module overview.
text: AIS training and competition nutrition education focuses on fueling for activity and recovery after training and competition. General food planning should consider the activity and practical access to food. This source is general education, not a condition-treatment diet or individualized calorie target.

title: AIS REST Hub — recovery
attribution: Australian Institute of Sport; short paraphrase of recovery overview.
text: AIS recovery education covers recovery nutrition and hydration alongside other recovery topics. Recovery is part of planning training. This overview does not establish medical clearance, diagnose pain, or prescribe treatment.

title: AIS — everyday recipe ideas
attribution: Australian Institute of Sport; source link for ordinary recipe ideas, not an allergy-safe menu.
text: AIS provides ordinary food recipe ideas. Food examples in this app are illustrative everyday combinations, not copied recipes or individualized nutrition prescriptions. Check actual ingredients and labels for allergies and cross-contact; a recipe source cannot establish that a food is safe for an individual.
